title: Survey of Orion Disks with ALMA (SODA). I. Cloud-level demographics of 873 protoplanetary disks
question: What is the disk dust mass distribution across 873 Class II protoplanetary disks in the L1641 and L1647 regions of the Orion A cloud, and how do median disk masses vary with position, YSO clustering, and compared to nearby star-forming regions?

what.value: Spitzer YSO catalog in Orion A

evidence.quote: We selected all Class II YSOs from (cite: megeath12) located in Orion A and below $-6^{\circ}$ degrees in declination, or above $\ell \sim 209.5^{\circ}$ degrees in Galactic longitude.

To correct for this effect, we refined the classifications from (cite: megeath12) to include the observations from the *Herschel* Orion Protostars Survey (HOPS) (cite: furlan16) at longer wavelengths, targeting embedded sources.

what.value: ALMA survey of 104 Herschel-detected Class II disks in L1641

evidence.quote: Recently, (cite: grant21) surveyed protoplanetary disks in L1641 with ALMA for the first time. Their sample consists of 104 Class II candidates from  that were also detected by *Herschel* at 70 $\mu$m.

what.value: Class III YSO catalog in L1641 from XMM-Newton

evidence.quote: In this section, we use the (cite: pillitteri13) catalog for Class III source numbers, and (cite: tobin20) for all embedded sources (Class I and 0).

what.value: Class 0 and Class I protostellar disk masses and numbers in Orion from VANDAM

evidence.quote: In this section, we use the (cite: pillitteri13) catalog for Class III source numbers, and (cite: tobin20) for all embedded sources (Class I and 0).

evidence.loc: Star-forming regions in Orion A and B
evidence.quote: Figure 13 extends this comparison between the SODA sample and Class II disk masses in other nearby star-forming regions, as well as the Class 0 and Class I disk mass distributions in Orion A and B presented by (cite: tobin20).

what.value: Upper Sco disk mass catalog and Class III/II ratio

evidence.quote: we artificially construct a sample of disks by randomly sampling (with replacement) disks from both the $\ell > 213.1^{\circ}$ area in Orion, and from the Upper Sco catalog published by (cite: barenfeld16).
Using a Class III to Class II ratio for Upper Sco of 4.2 (cite: luhman22) and $\sim 1$ for the southern L1641 sample leads to an $N_{III}/N_{II}$ ratio of $\sim 2$ for the mixed sample

what.value: Disk mass surveys of nearby star-forming regions (Lupus, Taurus, Cha I, rho Oph, CrA, OMC-2, ONC, NGC 2024, lambda Ori)

evidence.quote: This behavior was seen in surveys of disks at submillimeter wavelengths in the Taurus (cite: andrews13), Lupus (cite: ansdell16; ansdell18), and Chamaeleon I (cite: pascucci16) SFRs, as well as (more recently) the Corona Australis (cite: cazzoletti19) and $\rho$ Ophiuchus (cite: cieza19; williams19) regions.

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities and image continuum for all 882 pointings in parallel
recipe.method: Parallel calibration of 6 Scheduling Blocks using facility-provided scripts, extraction of individual target fields, and parallel deconvolution of each target combining all 4 continuum spectral windows

recipe.goal: Extract continuum fluxes and check for resolved emission
recipe.method: Search for brightest pixel within a 1.4" radius around catalog position; adopt 4 sigma detection threshold; fit double Gaussians to check for resolved emission
assumptions: Unresolved continuum emission for Class II disks

recipe.method: Convert 225 GHz continuum flux densities (and 4 sigma upper limits) to dust masses using optically thin greybody equation and interpolated Gaia DR2 distances
key_parameters: 16 galactic longitude bins (oversampled by factor of 2) for distance interpolation
assumptions: Optically thin 225 GHz dust continuum emission
Dust opacity kappa_230GHz = 2.3 cm^2 g^-1 with power-law index beta = 1

recipe.goal: Fit nonparametric and parametric disk mass distributions and compare populations
recipe.method: Estimate censored cumulative disk mass distributions using the Kaplan-Meier estimator, fit parametric log-normal and Weibull distributions, and compare distributions using log-rank tests
key_parameters: p = 0.05 cutoff for log-rank statistical significance
assumptions: Censoring is independent of disk mass for Kaplan-Meier, or underlying distribution is parametric (log-normal or Weibull)

recipe.goal: Analyze spatial variations along galactic longitude and identify YSO clusters
recipe.method: Bin sources into galactic longitude bins and identify 2D (RA, Dec) clusters using OPTICS algorithm; fit log-normal distributions to each bin/cluster and compare with Class III and embedded source fractions and simulated mixed populations
key_parameters: OPTICS min_samples = 5, minimum reachability steepness xi = 0.05, minimum cluster size = 50 members of Class II or earlier
10 longitudinal bins listed in Table (209.5 to 214.2 deg)
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio of 100 and 1 Myr evolution timescale from Class I to Class II for mass loss rate estimate
